turns.text: The list itself is not slow; the pointer chasing is. Each list_remove/list_push_front dereferences e->prev and e->next, which are scattered across the heap, so every touch is two cache misses. With 13k entries the node array is far bigger than L2, so you are memory-latency bound, not CPU bound. Two fixes: (1) store the list intrusively in one contiguous entry[] array and use 32-bit indices instead of pointers, so neighbors are often on the same cache line; (2) if you only need LRU-ish order, drop the list entirely and use a 2-bit counter array (the actual S3-FIFO small queue) with a periodic ghost sweep. Do you want the index-based node layout?
